http/body#

Message bodies: what a request or response carries, read once or many times.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

Response(status: Status.ok, content: TextBody(text: "hello"));
Response(status: Status.ok, content: JsonBody(Json(JsonField("id", 7))));
Response(status: Status.ok, content: BytesBody(bytes: image, media_type: "image/png"));
Request(url: url, method: Method.post, content: FormBody(QueryParameters(QueryParameter(name: "q", value: "tea"))));

let reading = request.body().reading();
let chunk = await reading.bytes(8192);      // [] at the end
reading.close();

Description#

Message bodies: what a request or response carries, read once or many times.

A BodyOpening describes a body; reading() starts one pass over it and gives a BodyReading. A replayable opening (bytes in memory) can be read again; a one-shot one (a socket) cannot, and a second reading() is BodyAlreadyOpened. An unknown length is UnknownBodyLength, never a negative number. Trailers are known only after the last byte.

Most code reads a whole body through Request.text(limit) or a client response's text() and json(), and writes one through a Content.

role BodyOpening#

role BodyOpening

Body openings describe a source; each reader owns one consumption lifetime. Unknown length is explicit and never represented by a negative sentinel.

object StreamBodyReading#

object StreamBodyReading does BodyReading, AsyncReading, Closing

Adopts an already body-delimited input and its exclusive owner. This is not a socket/message framer. Trailer metadata is published only at clean EOF. Pending storage is at most one Future and is cleared on every started exit.

StreamBodyReading.StreamBodyReading#

StreamBodyReading(input is AsyncReading, owner is Closing, trailers is Headers)

Reads input, closing owner when done; trailers are published at its end.
